content.text:
Based on my review:

- **stylist-view.tsx**: New `status === "limited"` branch renders `{props.limitMessage}` as JSX text content. React auto-escapes text nodes, so no XSS. No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no URL sinks, no shell/SQL/eval sinks.
- **stylist.tsx**: Stores `res.message` into React state and passes it to the view. Source traced to server action `app/generate/actions.ts:150` which pulls the string from `QuotaExceededError.message`, which in turn originates from `check.reason` inside `lib/outfits/quota.ts` — all server-controlled, not attacker-influenced.
- Authorization: the "limited" state is a UI outcome of a server-enforced check (`assertCanGenerate`). The client cannot bypass it by simulating this state — the enforcement lives on the server. The regenerate button only renders under `status === "ok"`, so no accidental re-invocation from the limited branch.
- Weather is intentionally preserved on limit; not an issue.
- Tests file: mock data only.

No security-relevant sinks are introduced, and no gating/authorization logic changes. No parser differentials, no allowlist changes, no PII/telemetry sinks touched.
